headline: October is the RECORD month for ship attacks in the Strait of Hormuz region
dek: 'October has seen the highest number of ship attacks on record' (Raydan): 28 confirmed + reported attacks in Strait of Hormuz and surrounding waters in October; 113 since the Feb 28 war began. IMO lists 120 incidents; 30+ supertankers (VLCCs) damaged including 11 in October = ~3.5% of the…
sources: Noam Raydan, Washington Institute for Near East Policy (incident map maintained since 2017); Reuters review of IMO list + MarineTraffic; Marisks (Greece consultancy); Bob McNally (Rapidan Energy); Helima Croft (RBC)
fault_line: Iran's blockade theater says the strait is closed and ships will 'burn'; the counting says Gulf exports are still above pre-war levels — is Hormuz a real blockade or a price machine?

sections.what_happened: 'October has seen the highest number of ship attacks on record' (Raydan): 28 confirmed + reported attacks in Strait of Hormuz and surrounding waters in October; 113 since the Feb 28 war began. IMO lists 120 incidents; 30+ supertankers (VLCCs) damaged including 11 in October = ~3.5% of the >900-ship global VLCC fleet. Rates >$1M/day. Marisks: 'October 2026 has emerged as the most intense period of maritime attacks in and around the Strait of Hormuz since the escalation of hostilities in March.' Brent $117.45 intraday Friday (settled $116.72, +10% on month); McNally warns $150 if critical infrastructure is hit.
sections.what_verified: Washington Institute's own incident-map dataset (primary data, tier-0 incident mapping); Reuters Oslo-datelined story reviewing IMO + MarineTraffic (Newswav mirror of Reuters piece); IMO incident list; Marisks corroborating 'most intense period' framing. Brent price = market data.
sections.what_disputed: IRGC's bigger claims (9 tankers in 36 hours incl. '7 tankers simultaneously') remain unverified — Trump called them fabricated; UKMTO verified only 3 strikes in that window (off Al-Faw Iraq, off Bukha Oman, off Limah Oman), none attributed; most struck vessels no longer report to UKMTO (Firebrand Project/Substack citing UKMTO + Washington Institute — attribution-only, T4). Kpler data (via Firebrand) says total Gulf oil exports remain above pre-war (24 vs 23.3 mbd) with strait-only flows ~82% of pre-war — the real constraint is price, not volume.
sections.why_matters: The numbers edition: 28 attacks, 113 since February, 3.5% of the world's supertankers damaged — but oil is still moving. The blockade story meets the flow data, and the fault line is the pocketbook: Brent at $117 and counting.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE (Hormuz by the Numbers franchise; NEW numbers this scan) -- Washington Institute/Reuters: October is the RECORD month for ship attacks in the Strait of Hormuz region — 28 confirmed+reported attacks in October, 113 since Feb 28; IMO 120 incidents; 30+ VLCCs damaged (11 in October), ~3.5% of global fleet; freight rates >$1M/day; Brent touched $117.45 Friday, settled $116.72

totw_analysis: Our read: The numbers edition: 28 attacks, 113 since February, 3.5% of the world's supertankers damaged — but oil is still moving. The blockade story meets the flow data, and the fault line is the pocketbook: Brent at $117 and counting. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Iran's blockade theater says the strait is closed and ships will 'burn'; the counting says Gulf exports are still above pre-war levels — is Hormuz a real blockade or a price machine?
